correctness.rationale: The actual increments start at one, and a nearest choice gives one while a farther choice flips the preceding increment. Hence depths never decrease, the newest vertex attains the height, and zero increments cannot be adjacent. Independence gives F_i(z)=z[p_i F_(i-1)(z)+(1-p_i)F_(i-2)(z)]. Reversal R_i(s)=s^i F_i(1/s) gives the determinant recurrence for R_n(-s): the off-diagonal product is s(1-p_i) and the diagonal is p_i (initial entry 1). In the interior, dividing by the positive diagonal on both sides gives a real symmetric weighted path; each eigenvector is determined by its first coordinate, so eigenvalues are simple. Bipartite symmetry gives exactly floor(n/2) nonzero positive/negative pairs and, for odd n, one zero. Reversing and normalizing at z=1 gives a product of r Bernoulli factors times z^h. Compactness of the Bernoulli parameter cube handles p_i=0 or 1. The deterministic odd-index resets make each even increment exactly its independent nearest-parent indicator, proving converse realization. At fixed mean, averaging two Bernoulli parameters raises every convex expectation by the nonnegative second-difference term; choosing the most separated pair at every step drives the parameter spread to zero (the sum of centered squares decreases by half the squared spread). The adjacent-integer secant proves the universal lower bound on integer-valued laws; both extremizers are realized by the reset schedules. The upper variance equality is equality in the sum-of-squares bound, and for the lower one the quadratic secant is strict off the adjacent integers, with the mean forcing a point mass when integral. A line segment between parameter vectors with the same sum realizes intermediate variances by continuity, including the degenerate cases. Independent finite corroboration: at n=8, for all 128 schedules with nearest weights 1/3 or 2/3, enumerated the 128 parent-choice histories per schedule and summed products of integer weights after clearing denominator 3^7; each vector of counts indexed by n minus the maximum depth equaled the reversed recurrence coefficients. This auxiliary check does not supply the general factorization; the frozen verify.py was read, not executed.

value.rationale: A full attainable-law description for a finite, geometrically defined random tree under independent time-varying probabilities is a natural structural result. It converts fixed-mean design into explicit schedules simultaneously bounding every convex loss and classifies the exact variance range, without misidentifying the actual increments as independent or claiming tail ordering.
